title: Consecutive Hand Groups
statement:
Check whether a hand of numbered cards can be dealt out completely into runs of consecutive values.

Contract
- `cards` is a non-null array of ints (duplicates allowed, possibly empty) and `groupSize` is the required size of every run.
- Every card must be used exactly once, in a group of exactly `groupSize` cards whose values are consecutive (`v, v + 1, ..., v + groupSize - 1`).
- Return `true` if such a split exists. An empty hand can be split trivially.
- Throw `IllegalArgumentException` when `groupSize` is less than 1. Do not mutate `cards`.

Examples
- `canGroup(new int[]{4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11}, 3)` returns `true` (runs 4-6 and 9-11).
- `canGroup(new int[]{1, 2, 3, 5}, 2)` returns `false`.
- `canGroup(new int[]{8}, 1)` returns `true`.
hints: If the number of cards is not a multiple of the group size, you can stop immediately.
The smallest remaining card can only be the start of a run, because nothing smaller is left to precede it.

Count the cards per value in an ordered map; repeatedly take the smallest key and remove one card from each of the next `groupSize` consecutive values, failing if one is missing. Intended complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space for n cards.
inputSyntax: Input: the cards, a semicolon, then the group size, for example: [4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11]; 3
